blocks.label: Overview
blocks.placeholder: We help small teams do their best work. This is an introduction to who we are, what we stand for, and how we show up in the world.

blocks.label: Who we are
blocks.placeholder: We started with a simple belief: good work should feel effortless. Today we make tools for teams who care about craft, used by people who would rather be making things than managing them.

blocks.label: What we stand for

points.textPlaceholder: We say and show things plainly. If it needs explaining, we simplify it.
Small things add up. We sweat the spacing, the wording and the timing.
We design for the person using it, on their busiest day, not for ourselves.

blocks.placeholder: Three beliefs sit behind everything we make and every decision in this guide.

blocks.label: About this guide
blocks.placeholder: This guide shows how the brand looks, sounds and behaves. Use it whenever you make something in our name, so everything we put into the world feels like it came from the same place.

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.placeholder: Memorable brands are built from the inside, out. Rooted in ideas around what our company stands for, it’s this vision that drives our visual identity, who we are and what we believe in.

blocks.label: Mission
blocks.placeholder: Our mission is to help small teams do their best work by removing the friction between having an idea and shipping it. We build tools that stay out of the way, so the people using them can focus on what matters.

blocks.label: Brand
blocks.placeholder: We believe good work should feel effortless. Everything we make, from the product to the way we write, is designed to be clear, calm and considered. This idea underpins the whole identity.

blocks.label: Logos
blocks.placeholder: Our logo is the most visible expression of the brand. It comes in four forms, each suited to a different amount of space. Use the lockup wherever there is room, and the symbol on its own only where the name is already clear.

blocks.label: Clearspace
blocks.placeholder: Give the logo room to breathe. Keep a clear area around every side, measured with the symbol as the unit, and never let type, images or other marks cross into it.

blocks.label: Logo colors
blocks.placeholder: The logo appears in a single color taken from the palette, chosen for contrast against its background. Never recolor it outside the palette, and never place it on a background it can’t be read against.

blocks.label: Palette
blocks.placeholder: Our palette is small on purpose. The first color leads and appears most; the others support it. Use them in the proportions shown here, and take values from the tiles rather than sampling them from screen.

blocks.label: Proportion
blocks.placeholder: Roughly how much of each color appears across a piece. The lead color carries most of the weight; the others are there to support and accent it.

blocks.label: Contrast
blocks.placeholder: Pairings that stay legible. Each is checked against the WCAG standard: AAA and AA work for text at any size, AA Large only for headings and large type.

blocks.label: Color modes
blocks.placeholder: No color system shows the full range of what we see. Each mode suits a medium: RGB and Pantone give the most vibrant color on screen and in print, while CMYK covers everyday printing with some loss of range.

Vibrant, the preferred method for printing

blocks.label: Typeface
blocks.placeholder: One family does the work across the brand. It is clean, clearly legible and made for screens, with enough character in the display sizes to feel like ours.

blocks.label: Try it
blocks.placeholder: Set anything in the typeface. Change the size and weight to see how it behaves at every scale.

blocks.label: Hierarchy
blocks.placeholder: Hierarchy tells people what to read first. We build it with size and weight, then position, capitals and color. Use these steps and nothing in between.

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.placeholder: We move on one curve and three timings. Small things are quick, most moves take the base timing, and big moments are slow. Keep to those and almost everything will feel like us.

blocks.label: Principles
blocks.placeholder: Three ideas behind every move. Everything else in this section follows from them.

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.placeholder: Our photography is honest and unstaged. We shoot real people and real places in natural light, with calm compositions and room around the subject, so every image feels observed rather than arranged.

blocks.label: Principles

points.textPlaceholder: Daylight, from a window or outdoors. Soft shadows, no flash and no colored gels.
People doing what they actually do, in places they actually work. Nothing posed for the camera.
One clear subject with space around it, so type and the logo have somewhere to sit.

blocks.placeholder: Three qualities make a photograph ours. Check a new image against each of them before it is used.

blocks.label: Style
blocks.placeholder: A small set of images that sets the tone. New photography should sit comfortably beside these.

blocks.label: Treatment
blocks.placeholder: How an image is shot and finished. These settings keep photographs from different shoots looking like one set.

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.placeholder: Illustration explains what a photograph can’t. Ours is flat and geometric, drawn from the shapes in the symbol and colored from the palette, and used where an idea needs simplifying rather than decorating.

blocks.label: Style
blocks.placeholder: A small set of illustrations that sets the style. New drawings should look like they belong to this family.

blocks.label: Depth
blocks.placeholder: Gradients and layering give a flat drawing depth. A gradient runs between two brand colors, or from the subject into the background, never into a color outside the palette.

blocks.label: Texture
blocks.placeholder: A fine grain adds warmth to large flat areas. Keep it around one pixel, apply it to whole shapes or the whole drawing, and never let it soften an edge.

blocks.label: Patterns
blocks.placeholder: Patterns built from the illustration shapes, in palette colors. Use them as backgrounds and bands, never behind body text.

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.placeholder: Icons help people find their way. Ours are simple, drawn on one grid with one stroke, and used to support the words around them rather than replace them.

blocks.label: Icons
blocks.placeholder: Our icons are designed to complement the symbol. They share the same corners, clean lines and simple shapes, so they feel like part of one family wherever they appear.

blocks.label: Icon grid
blocks.placeholder: Every icon is drawn on the same grid with the same stroke. The keylines guide consistent proportions across different shapes.

items.placeholder: Simple shapes that read at a glance.
One stroke weight across the whole set.

blocks.label: Principles
blocks.placeholder: A few qualities run through the whole set. New icons should follow them so they sit comfortably next to the rest.

blocks.label: Sizes
blocks.placeholder: Icons are drawn for a small set of sizes. Use these sizes rather than scaling freely, so strokes stay crisp and consistent.

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.placeholder: How we write is as much a part of the brand as how we look. Our words should feel like they come from one person: someone clear, warm and sure of what they are saying.

placeholder.description: We say what we mean in as few words as it takes. One idea at a time, with the most useful thing first.
We write to one person, not an audience. We are on their side, and it shows in how we explain things.
We make a recommendation and stand behind it. If something went wrong, we say so and say what happens next.

blocks.label: Writing tips

points.textPlaceholder: Read it out loud. If a sentence sounds stiff, rewrite it the way you would say it.
Put the most useful thing first. Background and detail can follow.
People are busy. If you can say the same thing in fewer words, do.
No hedging. Readers should be able to rely on what we tell them.
points.titlePlaceholder: Say it like you mean it

points.textPlaceholder: A launch and an error are different moments. Keep the voice and adjust the tone.
